answer: Operator-Bound Cost Amplification. Each identity registers with a cheap cipher commitment, but every action emits a signed lantern beacon tying it to the operator's execution environment. A prism process clusters beacons by shared runtime fingerprints; when a cluster exceeds a diversity threshold, all its identities enter a probation state where each action triggers a capped but rising fee drawn from the operator's settlement balance. Attacker cost scales with cluster size, so N sybils pay roughly N times the per-identity fee while honest single operators stay below the cap.
